data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Design by Contract typically operates on method calls and class invariants in a closed system, whereas artifact admission may involve open, evolving domains with external evidence.","Contract composition in DbC is well-defined via inheritance; composition of artifact admission contracts may not follow the same rules."],"overturn_conditions":["If empirical study shows that per-artifact contract checks do not correlate with overall system correctness in this domain, the analogy fails.","If the system's correctness depends on cross-artifact relational constraints that DbC does not naturally handle, the transferred test strategy is insufficient."],"shared_structure":["Both systems involve a collection of items (artifacts / objects) that must satisfy defined contracts.","In both, correctness can be partially verified by checking each item against its contract independently."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["The practice of writing per-element contract assertions in DbC transfers to writing per-artifact admission checks in the artifact-set problem.","The principle that contracts should be explicit and checkable transfers directly."]},"claim":"The test should verify per-element contract validity (each artifact satisfies its admission contract) rather than asserting a total count, transferring Design by Contract principles to the artifact-set problem.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the analogy to Design by Contract is disanalogous in that artifact contracts do not compose cleanly to guarantee set-level properties, per-element testing may miss emergent set-level failures.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the domain requires relational constraints between artifacts (not just per-element), this approach fails to catch violations.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Drawing an analogy to Design by Contract (SRC_008), the test checks that each committed artifact meets the preconditions and invariants required by its contract. This ensures the integrity of the admitted set at the element level, making the test robust to set growth. The mechanist school stance (SRC_001) supports this by focusing on the internal mechanism (contract checking) that guarantees correctness regardless of set size.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
